units.summary: A model call runs in one of two modes the user picks per use, on the device (the user's own local model, nothing leaves the vault) or in the cloud with the user's own key (a scoped slice sent from the device straight to the provider); no server sees either, the device is preferred, and a call is never upgraded to the cloud silently.
There is no chat; the assistant has no conversation surface and keeps no conversation memory, asking and writing happen inside module screens, and acting happens through outside agents.

A module's ask and write help is a shipped, consent-gated capability block on its screens that runs the mode choice and the review of what is sent; a module's named pipeline (reading a page, extracting a syllabus, drafting, advising) stays a scoped one-shot model call, never an agent.

The runtime answers the mediated ask by reaching the user's local model or, through Integrations' mediator, a cloud provider with the user's key; until it exists every call reads unavailable and every module's manual path keeps working.
Until encryption lands, the web product runs the assistant only on the user's own local model; cloud mode with a key runs only on the desktop app, where the key lives in the system keychain.

Local models are set up by the user, and Vida ships user documentation for it (the parameters, the specifications and where everything goes); which models and providers come first and how prompts and redaction are built are decided in the build.
Vida runs no model of its own; it hosts none, ships no first-party assistant and offers no attested cloud mode.
Agents are the user's own, created and run in third-party tools; Vida creates, hosts and runs no agent loop, and one or several outside agents read and write in Vida only through its gateway.

The gateway is the sandbox that Vida's assistant feature owns; every outside agent's call is checked against that agent's grants, waits for approval, is logged and can be undone, and it shares the grant engine with user-written capabilities, which keep their own code runner (CB-11).

One central tool registry lists every tool an outside agent can be granted; a tool is a capability action a module offers, every module offers tools for asking, writing and acting, and a tool missing from the registry can't be granted.

An outside agent asks for everything; each planned change waits in the approval prompt, where the user approves, edits or rejects it, unless the user set an auto-grant for a run, a session or a connection (local or by key).

An assistant connection is configured per provider (mode, provider, default scope and the requested no-train flag) and carries no key; the key is custodied by Integrations and never reaches a module, a capability or an agent.
The activity log records every tool call an agent makes and its result, plus what was sent to a cloud model, and the user can undo one agent run as a single step.

In the permissions editor the user sets each agent's envelope module by module and its limits per grant (allow, limit or enforce whatever they want); Vida ships no fixed budget, and the gateway enforces what the user set.
Outside agents reach the gateway on every product shape in a way the user approves, never through a Vida server.

Each use asks where the call runs (on the device, nothing leaves, or the cloud with the named provider), and before a cloud call the user sees exactly what will be sent, can remove or redact parts, and nothing is sent until they confirm.
The assistant has its own management page, apart from Integrations, listing the user's providers and local model with mode, default scope and the no-train request; a key is never shown.
When a capability or an agent asks for permissions, a grant prompt shows what it may read, what it may do and whether anything may leave the device, and the grant can be revoked later.

The assistant has three stores, the per-provider connections (no key), the cloud-call audit and the agent activity log; there is no conversation store, and the rows are field-encrypted once encryption lands.

A cloud model call is an egress through Integrations' egress guard (per-target consent, the union when a sensitive read joins, an audit and never automatic), and the assistant forwards only the slice its caller gives; redaction trims what is sent but never makes a call private about its own subject.

An agent's callable tools are exactly its granted envelope; a tool outside it fails closed, the agent holds no ambient authority, its writes go through the module's guarded write interface, and a model call it needs is the mediated ask, so it never holds a key.

Prompt injection is bounded; content from an untrusted origin carries its provenance into the prompt (an unknown origin is untrusted), and an injected tool call still meets the tool gate and the egress gate, so it can't widen the scope or invent a target.
A row a model wrote carries source ai, stamped by the owning module's own service, and is encrypted like any vault row once encryption lands; the assistant drafts and the user owns.

Cloud mode's disclosure says plainly that the provider sees the chosen slice in plaintext, the user's address and key identity and a profile across calls, and that no-train is requested, never guaranteed.

Vida answers only for leaks from its own security, never for what a provider the user chose does with what was sent; Vida documents and shows the safest ways to use its assistant (the local model, reviewing what is sent) and says plainly that nothing involving data can be guaranteed.

Vida's assistant is a helper across all of Vida, like Notion with Claude, never a feature of one module; every module gets it with three kinds of help, asking across the user's data, writing inside pages and acting through tools.

A book's title, author, isbn, review and cover, a chapter's title, an asset's file reference, a bookmark's label, a highlight's captured text, a quote's text and every page photo are encrypted client-side [E]; enums, page numbers, positions, dates and counters are plaintext. Book files and page photos are client-encrypted attachments. M1 is a pass-through.

A reading session is a base session (the reading sub_type by default) plus a Books-owned extension keyed by session_id, never its own table; manual capture records time, pages and the stop point, digital capture a granular position and statistics, and a page photo is read for position and always stored encrypted as a visual reading journal shown in the daily journal.

A plan covers one or many books, sequenced (one after another) or parallel (the quota split); its goal is set by hand or calculated to a target (a date, a weekday or a day of the month) and is a pursuable target; a missed day, week or month reshapes the plan and proposes how to catch up, never dropping the target silently.
Books owns reading plans; the study planner and every other consumer reads plans, deadlines and sessions and never writes them, and the Calendar reconciles while Books handles only its own end.

The Education partition links books and subjects through a many-to-many junction and a Books read contract; Education reads books per subject and their pace against the next class or assessment, Books reads subject schedules and assessment dates to pace the student ahead, and neither reads the other's tables.

Integrations never touch the zero-knowledge core; the isbn lookup is a device-mediated public-reference fetch under the external-in grant, revocable, and speech, transcription and photo reading are scoped model calls on device or in the cloud, never agents, with derived rows marked source=ai; each is opt-in behind a consent step and keeps a manual fallback.

The Reader is core and in-app; one surface with three modes (read, listen including speech-converted files, annotate live in every mode) on all three platforms, files never leave the encrypted store to be read, and opening an asset starts a reading session.

Publisher, genre and category are Books-scoped entity_tags, never columns; a book's summary and key takeaways are notes with their own per-type views; skill and purpose links are owned by Skills and Purposes; the book row stays lean.
Every view ships a default; books with only a table of contents, books with no copy, unsynced mappings and empty shelves render gracefully and invite the next step.
Every write (a position, an annotation, a session, a plan) succeeds locally first; sync is last-writer-wins per entity, and files ride the attachment pipeline.

Books has a Reading Hub (current reads, today's quotas and pace, resume, recent bookmarks and quotes, statistics, plan alerts), a Bookshelf (gallery, list or table, by tag, status and format), All Plans and each plan's page, the All Quotes library, a tabbed Book Hub (an Education tab once a subject is linked), the physical companion mode, and the add-book and plan wizards with conflict prompts in context.

A book is the work and exists without any copy; it has zero or more per-format assets, each with its own native position (a page, an e-book location or an audio timestamp), and a physical or braille asset holds a position the user enters.

Each Books capability renders its terminal states (loading, empty with a call to action, a typed error with retry, populated); a broken file never renders as an empty book, an unreachable target shows the catch-up options, and an unresolved conflict is flagged.

Books has its own blocks (capability entries with an inline target), such as the books being read with a resume action, today's quotas, the day's page photos and a quote; each reads Books live and writes only through the Books service, so the journal and any page can show and work on them.

Books' journal contribution answers a date with that day's pages read, reading sessions logged and the plans on pace or behind, empty on an idle day; it is registered into the journal registry through registerBooksJournal.

Books feeds the Sessions due agenda with each active plan's quota for the day and its target date, so the Global Calendar, the journal agenda and the study planner see reading quotas without copying them.
Books serves a read provider for books in the shared view registry, so the Bookshelf's saved views and any view or session that targets a book resolve it instead of degrading.

Books advertises each book's reading progress in the measurement source registry, so a Purposes goal or a reading plan's pursuable target derive-pulls it; a conflicted or unmeasured book reads null, and Books stores no measurement axes.
Editing a plan's quota or target mid-plan runs the same recalculation as a missed quota.
The Bookshelf filters books by status, tag, owned format and linked subject, and the All Quotes library filters quotes by tag, each through the Books service.
Books reads the quote-embed toggles (global and per book), the conflict rule and the Reader and companion defaults from Preferences through its narrow port, never its own store.
A book and a chapter are entity link targets; Knowledge objects, Skills and Purposes own their links to books, and Books authors none of them.

A book's unified progress is derived from its assets' positions through the cross-format mapping under the conflict rule (BK-8), never hand-set as a separate truth; books.progress is a nullable override (null derives), never a counter that defaults to zero.

In the app the composition root builds Books with its deps (spaces, notes, sessions, the session registry) and calls registerBooks so the reading sub_type exists; it passes the Preferences port (BK-28) and the effects rail with its reachable registry, and later the ingestion, attachment and model ports; it registers the due lane (BK-23), the book read provider (BK-24) and the measure source (BK-25), and passes Books to Education as its books port.

The data-model record shows the ten Books tables (assets, the three annotation tables, the reading session extension, plans and their books, the subject junction), progress as a nullable override, and the retired format, current page, genre and tags columns.

Book status, asset format, annotation kind, plan arrangement, goal type and conflict rule are closed enums declared once (string unions, `CHECK` constraints and `Zod` schemas); the mapping state (synced, pending, failed) joins them with the mapping.

A completed reading session emits one measurement signal for its book and never an economy grant; whether reading earns a grant is Gamification's rule on the base session, and the reading sub_type declares no effect today.

The book dataset (metadata, covers, page counts, tables of contents and classification) ships with Vida as an opt-in public-reference default that the user accepts or declines; it refreshes as a whole set and is read from a local copy, and picking a book from it fills the work, its chapters and its tags in one step, never one item fetched at a time; hand entry always stays.

Every reading is a session; opening the Reader, the companion mode or a routine step starts one through Sessions, the user can name it and choose its type (reading by default) as Sessions allows, and Books records its capture on that session.

Positions map between formats automatically, from a transcription and table-of-contents anchors near the stopped point, never by manual calibration; while the mapping is pending, failed or absent, the user sees the native position and an explicit "not synced yet" state, and a mapped position is never guessed.

Bookmarks, highlights and quotes anchor to the work and show from every asset through the mapping (a bookmark at minute 52 of the audiobook appears on the mapped page); under an unsynced mapping they show at their native position with the BK-4 state, and removing an asset never removes them.

There are three annotation natures; a highlight is a light span marker in digital content with no notes and no links, while bookmarks and quotes take notes as pages and link to each other; quotes are stored per book.
Any note or page can embed a stored quote by reference, never a copy; embedding is toggled globally and per book, and the per-book toggle overrides the global one.

A clash between position sources (assets, photo capture) is asked of the user in context by default; the user may preset a rule (a chosen source of truth, the last valid one, or the photo) that then resolves it automatically, and an unresolved clash shows unified progress as conflicted, never either value.

The table of contents is a flat chapter list owned by Books and usable before owning a copy, entered by hand or by an isbn or metadata lookup; the syllabus and schedule are Education's and meet the table of contents only through the partition (BK-13).

One open capability registry holds every capability definition, shipped ones registered in code and the user's persisted and synced; Knowledge's study methods are a kind of it, not a parallel registry.

An untrusted capability touches only the entities it's attached to, writes only through module write interfaces with no double count, needs explicit consent for sensitive modules (Finance, Health), and is a strict subset of what shipped capabilities may do.

User capability code runs in a sandbox with no ambient authority (no direct database, network, file system or other capabilities' state), reaching Vida only through the mediated capability interface, and is marked untrusted and can't claim a shipped id.

Zero knowledge holds under authoring; media a capability captures is encrypted, there is no ambient network, external reach is declared, consented and mediated, and a sensitive read combined with egress needs both consents.
The envelope and its invariants are the same on every platform, a definition and its grant sync together, and a device that can't enforce the envelope refuses to run the capability.
A grant is never permanent; revoking it syncs and the capability stops on its next call.
The sandbox enforces processor time, memory and wall-clock budgets and terminates a runaway capability, so the local app never hangs.

Capabilities can be code and in-depth personalization engines (a video playlist, levels tied to a Skills hub), and the user connects them, with other modules' features, into new features inside a Space.
A standalone placement is a block_instances row on a Space surface, created, configured and removed through a placement service and rendered with its declared terminal states.
Community capability blocks and curated libraries come in as imports over the Integrations feature, never a marketplace, and run as untrusted.
A capability declares its render targets (inline, standalone or both), and the user picks each placement among them.

A capability is a plugin with six parts (identity and kind, config, entity bindings scoped to what it's attached to, render targets, emitted signals, and universal properties, so it's taggable, linkable and attachable).

A capability writes only through the target module's documented write interface under the guarded-write contract, and a timed or measurable outcome drives a session, which owns the effects; a pure-render capability emits nothing.

A standalone placement on a Space is drawn from that Space's offered palette, an inline placement from the union of the page's Spaces and the editor base, and curating the palette gates adding without removing existing placements.
Every capability declares loading, empty, error and success for each render target it supports.
Shipped capabilities are trusted and every other one, user-authored or arriving in an imported template, is untrusted; there is no promotion to trusted.
An untrusted capability declares what it needs, the user grants that envelope, and only the granted set is allowed; nothing is implicit and every unknown denies.
A capability whose declared envelope changes fails closed until the user grants it again, so privilege never grows silently.

A check-in's intentions, wins, gratitude, challenges, tomorrow's focus, reflection and custom answers, and a template's name, description and question labels and placeholders, are encrypted client-side [E]; mood, energy, the type, the date and the schedule stay plaintext for the trend charts. M1 is a pass-through.
Check-ins are hard-deleted with no foreign keys; deleting a template keeps its check-ins with their template cleared and removes its questions, in application code.

Check-ins owns its streak, derived on read from the check-ins and never written to user_profile; a completion emits the reward feeder that Gamification applies to the consequence ledger, and Check-ins never writes points itself.
Every check-in and template edit succeeds locally first, and structured columns sync last-writer-wins.

Check-ins' journal contribution answers a date with that day's check-ins (which slots are done, mood and energy), empty on a day with none; it is registered into the journal registry through a Check-ins journal registration helper, which does not exist yet.

Check-ins has its own blocks (capability entries with an inline target), such as today's check-in slots with a start action, the mood and energy trend and the streak; each reads Check-ins live and writes only through the Check-ins service, so the journal and any page can show and work on them.

Check-ins has an entry wizard that renders the active template for the chosen type, a standalone page with the history list, a calendar and a trends dashboard tab, a standalone editor per template with its schedule, and the review screens; the daily entry also opens from the journal.

Each Check-ins capability renders its terminal states (loading, empty with a call to action, a typed error with retry, populated); a failed save reverts with a typed error and never loses an entry, and a failed trend or streak shows a flagged partial, never a wrong number.
Check-ins feeds the Sessions due agenda with each scheduled check-in and review for the day at its preferred time, so the Global Calendar and the journal agenda show them without copying them.
Check-ins serves a read provider for check-ins in the shared view registry, so a saved view and anything that targets a check-in resolve it instead of degrading.

Check-ins advertises mood, energy, completion and the streak in the measurement source registry, so a Purposes goal with a check-in contributor, Gamification's streak read and Health derive-pull them; Check-ins stores no measurement axes.

There is one check-in per date and type, so morning, afternoon, evening and the reviews coexist on a day; a second check-in for a taken slot is a typed DuplicateCheckInError, never an overwrite, and the slot is immutable on update.
Preferences gates check-in reminders with their own push toggle, keyed so the toggle matches the reminder's due rows; there is no Check-ins toggle today.
A custom answer is checked against its question; a scale or rating outside its bounds, or an answer of the wrong kind for its field type, is a typed validation error.

The template and question library ships with Vida as an opt-in default dataset the user accepts or declines; it refreshes as a whole set and is read from a local copy, and picking a template copies it into the user's own templates.
The user can delete a check-in; it is removed for good with its journal day-page link.

In the app the composition root builds Check-ins with the notes service as its journal link and the effects rail with its registry; it registers the journal contribution (CK-13), the due lane (CK-17), the read provider (CK-18) and the measure sources (CK-19).
The data-model record shows the three Check-ins tables as built, the composite unique slot, six types, no foreign keys and no deleted_at, and the streak gone from user_profile.

Check-in type, question field type, schedule type and preferred time are closed enums declared once (string unions, `CHECK` constraints and `Zod` schemas), and mood and energy are integers from 1 to 10.
The check-in type is one of six, morning, afternoon, evening, weekly_review, monthly_review and yearly_review.

Each check-in type has a ready default template, so the user checks in with zero setup; the check-in's standard columns are the built-in default template, and custom_data holds only the answers to extra questions the user added, never a copy of a standard field.

A template owns ordered, typed questions (mood_scale, energy_scale, text_list, text_area, rating, boolean) with a field key unique per template; a required question blocks completion until answered, and min_value and max_value bound a scale or rating answer.

A weekly, monthly or yearly review reads Purposes, Projects and Tasks progress through their services, never their tables, holds the Purpose target review, and backlinks what it covered; a failed read shows what is available with a flag, never a falsely complete review, and a review with nothing linked saves as free reflection.
A check-in links to its day's journal page through entity_links, never a copy of its answers, and editing a past check-in re-feeds its day page.
A template's schedule (daily, weekly or custom days and a preferred time), set in its own editor, fires the check-in reminders through Preferences and Notifications.
Check-ins carry no tags; they relate to other entities only through entity_links, a deliberate opt-out from the shared entity_tags.

The Global Calendar is a Vida feature of its own with its own page, owned by no module; it is the book of the user's life read by date, showing every module's dated items in six ranges (Year, Month, Week, Day, Agenda, Living), and it owns no table and stores no copy.
Living draws each active habit as a thread across the week, kept, missed, today, future or a rest day that is never a miss, with its current streak beside it.
Living shows the week's hours by the purpose each block serves, in the purpose's colour, and flags a purpose with none; a purpose with no measure reads unmeasured, never a made-up number.
Living offers today's open time, the free availability windows from now to the end of the day after the day's exceptions, as an offer to slot deep work, study or a habit.
Living flags a slipping task (overdue, or scheduled after its due date) in today's column, and shows how many times a must-do was pushed once Tasks keeps its reschedule history.
A future day in Living shows the user's intention for it, read from their check-ins.

The Calendar reads every module's due work through the Sessions due agenda, one call per visible span, and never names a module; a task sits on its due and scheduled dates, another module's item on its deadline date, and review due work arrives through its owner's lane, never a direct review read.

Each lane shows its own loading, empty, error and success, one lane failing greys only that lane, nothing is ever made up, and a module's failed due lane reads unavailable right now, never as nothing due.
Sessions' placed blocks render as the plan beside the deadlines, timed in Week and Day and in Agenda, and past focus shows on each past day; nothing writes planned blocks yet.
Every day the Calendar shows is a day in the user's timezone, and it reads the user's time format and week start from Preferences, with one 12-hour time shape across every range.

Every range renders and never writes; a check, a move or slotting open time is an intent the owning module's capability carries out, and with no capability composed the control is absent, never a dead one.

Events stay each module's own (Relationships events, project events, Health's scheduled items); when two modules hold the same event they are connected by a link, never copied or given one owner, and the Calendar reads each through its owner and shows the connection.

Outside calendars (a class schedule feed, external appointments) arrive through Integrations into the module that owns them and render on the Calendar like any lane, and the Calendar can be exported as a feed; on the localhost product there is no server, so a fetch runs on the device.

The Calendar keeps its own page and lens rather than being a saved view; the calendar layout of saved views is separate, and ADR-007 §3.5 and its review trigger are amended to say so, including whether provider fan-out holds its interaction budget.

From the Calendar the user ticks a habit, slots open time, reserves a slot for an activity and moves a placed block, each through the owning module's capability composed into the Calendar (Habits, Sessions availability and planned blocks, Routines slot presets); the Calendar owns no slot or reservation record.

A range switcher (a toolbar of the six ranges that condenses to a menu below tablet width) with previous, today and next sits in the page frame, which owns the period title once; the range swap fades and Today pulses the today mark, both instant under reduced motion; the active range and focused date are page state, never stored.

Month reuses the shared month grid without its own header, shows the period's due items as chips with today marked and named, and a dense day unfurls in place, one day at a time, collapsing on Escape, a second press or a month change.

Agenda lists the focused week's days in provider order, grouping only today by daypart (morning before noon, afternoon to 18:00, evening after, an untimed item in the morning); an item shows its time or All day, Must for an obligation task and no weight otherwise, a struck title when done, and habits by their time of day.

Week and Day are one time-column view (Day is one column) with an hour gutter, one all-day strip and timed blocks placed by hour in side-by-side lanes when they overlap; only items with a real clock time become blocks, so a task or a habit is never given a time.
Year shows twelve mini-months with a density dot per day (has items, or busy when Month would hide some), today ringed and the current month accented; a month's heading opens that month.

Living shows the focused week by temporal asymmetry, a past day as record (the journal page's first paragraph, what was completed, the focus logged), today as live (its items, open time, slipping tasks and an uncompleted relationships item carried forward from earlier in the week) and a future day as intention and plan; each lane degrades alone.

The tier follows the notification's nature and the platform; a time-based reminder on a native device is a local scheduled alert, a time-based reminder on the web and any event use the wake signal, and in-app underlies all three.
The engine executes an already-gated delivery decision; channel, permission and quiet-hours gating is the dispatcher's, and governing the server relay's transmit is the server's.
No port makes a network call before real reach; the engine decides when and to whom, never what, and authors no schema, so real reach replaces the ports with no signature change.

Each product shape delivers a time-based reminder its own way; the localhost web product the user runs on their machine delivers it locally, with no server; the desktop and mobile apps register each upcoming reminder with the native local scheduler ahead of its time, with quiet hours baked in per the user's shift or suppress choice, and reschedule (cancel and re-register) when the schedule or the quiet hours change; only the server product, which serves the web and manages its information, adds the wake signal.

With the server product, the wake signal reaches closed devices; on a blob's arrival the server's wake relay sends a content-minimal push to the user's registered devices (push tokens on the device registry), the device syncs and composes the notification locally, the web the server serves uses a service worker with Web Push, and email sends the generic nudge.
Only the wake-signal tier reaches off the device (push wake-only and the generic email); local scheduled alerts and in-app compose on the device, and `sms` is never a channel.
The wake payload carries the owner's routing only and refuses at run time any content, type or subject key with PayloadNotContentFree, never a silent strip.
Quiet hours are baked in when a local alert is registered (shifted or suppressed per the user's policy), since a pre-scheduled alert fires with the dispatcher not running.
A reschedule diffs the registered alerts by their dedup key, cancels the dropped, registers the new and leaves the unchanged alone.
The dedup key passes an event's effect_event_id through unchanged and keys a due reminder by its due occurrence id, namespaced so the two never collide.
A durable row materializes only when the occurrence's time has arrived, never written ahead with a future date.
Any external port that doesn't deliver (the deny-safe default included) folds back to in-app and flags it; in-app is the unconditional baseline and a delivery never rejects.
In the no-third-party mode the engine never calls an off-device port (no push service, no email, no relay), even if the decision lists those channels.
Every emitted value (a style variable, a theme token, a theme key) traces to exactly one seed entry, and no value is authored twice.
Text on every surface meets the minimum text contrast in every preset and mode, checked in the build over the full matrix.
Motion tokens are four durations within the standard's bands and three easing curves plus linear, routed to the style variables and a typed motion export.
Every animation has a reduced-motion path that changes state instantly, and animates transform, opacity or clip-path only.

The user picks one of three preset families (editorial, reader or quiet desk), each a palette and a font pair over the editorial base in light and dark, named scheme first, and the pipeline builds no other family.
A preset's fonts switch through a style-variable seam set on the page root, instantly and with no transition.
The scheme is set on the page root and the preset on the body, so dialogs and menus rendered outside the app tree take the preset too.
Density (calm or dense) is one stylesheet toggled by an attribute, scaling the spacing band and the type together.
Components read preset colours through the semantic tokens, and only signal colours, which don't change per preset, stay on the base component themes.
The theme configuration composes only generated outputs, dark is a switchable theme set through the provider, and the web animates through style transitions fed by the motion tokens.
Fonts are self-hosted with only the default face preloaded, and the chrome fonts ship with the chrome role.

Tokens are three layers that never skip one; primitives are literals, semantics reference primitives and components reference semantics, and a literal outside the primitives, a skipped layer, a dangling reference or an empty layer fails the build with its cause named.
The token values are Vida's brand, replacing the placeholder palette, with the full contrast matrix re-run.
The token set covers what components need, component tokens, enter and exit transition presets, font weight and spacing keys and a scrim opacity token, so no component holds a raw value.
Storybook is the design system, holding every component and full-interface surface as envisioned, not only what the first release needed.
A community-forkable design file mirrors the code-first design system, synced through the design tool's agent server and a scripter, never Tokens Studio.
Names follow each target's own scheme; a seed path a/b/c is the style variable --a-b-c, and theme tokens follow the theme library's flat categories.
The same seed always builds byte-identical outputs.
Every output is generated and marked as never hand-edited; the seed is the only editable input.
The scales are complete with no arbitrary values; brand and neutral ten-step ramps, success and danger signals, seven type sizes, the 4-point spacing set, radius from small to full and three shadows.
Dark is designed in parallel, never inverted; every semantic that differs in dark has its own dark entry, mapping one to one to design-tool modes.
Every spacing primitive sits on the 4-point grid, and an off-grid one fails the build.
Typography and shadow tokens skip the theme tokens and go to the style variables plus a typed export each.
A consequence dispatches typed effects on the rail; the economy's effects are all Additive, each appending its own output row keyed by a deterministic effect event key.
A locked amount is recoverable; a release appends a compensating row that returns it to current, never a delete.
A currency declares a backing kind of real money, self-granted or measured time; experience points are one currency, not privileged.
Earned, locked, spent and distributed recompute on read from the consequence ledger, and current is earned minus locked minus spent; stored counters are caches, never truth.
To-distribute is a configured ceiling minus what has been distributed, not a ledger sum, and is null with no ceiling.
A penalty writes a recoverable lock row; the ledger is append-only, with corrections as compensating rows, and the below-floor clamp and flag belong to the enforcing surface.

The grant and lock handlers write one ledger row inside the rail's transaction, unique on the effect event key, kind and target; the rail's applied-effects log guards replay, and the ledger's unique key converges devices.
The consequence coordinator fans a fire out to the rail per typed effect, with no new write path and no new idempotency.

The economy owns currencies, the ledger, the four derived quantities, lock-not-destroy, the coordinator and the effect classes; it does not own the rail, conditions (a condition is a measurement binding) or the sandbox.
The user spends a currency (redeems an allowance) and distributes from its pool through ledger rows keyed by a deterministic event key, and a spend clamps at the floor.

Education's names and free text (a subject's title, description, provider, instructor, url and metadata; a feed's url, name and last error; a synced event's summary, description, location and raw event; every hierarchy, grading, assessment and vault name or description) are encrypted client-side; enums, dates, scores, progress and counters stay plaintext.

Subject and program progress lives in an Education-only measure, its kind and binding mode on the Projects axes but separate storage, a nullable override that derives on read (a subject from its grade, a program by rolling up its subjects), and unmeasured reads null, never zero.

A curriculum is user-shaped and forkable; a fork deep-copies the live terms and subjects into a new tree with a lineage pointer, remaps their refs and resets progress, never writes the base, and deleting a fork leaves the base.
Terms are hierarchical time containers (year, semester, term) with an optional parent that must resolve when given, and they're optional.
Each subject has one vault holding its documents (inline when small, an attachment reference when large) and its notes together, and a write succeeds locally first.
From subject down to topic, Education's data is progressively fillable; pages render partial data gracefully and invite increments, and empty is never an error.
Every personalizable Education view ships a sensible default so the user isn't lost personalizing instead of studying.
Every Education write succeeds locally first, and Education tags its programs, curricula and subjects through the shared entity tags, never an inline tags column.

Below the subject, a subject holds modules and a module holds topics, the planning topics Knowledge objects link to and that assessments, homework and study sessions target; deleting a planning topic never deletes acquired knowledge.

Education's surfaces show their terminal states (the programs dashboard, every hub tab, the curriculum, grading-system and schedule builders, calendar feed sync, assessment entry, the subject page and its vault), each with loading, empty, typed error and success.

Education has a programs dashboard (acing and lacking areas), a hub with a tab per entity and user-chosen view modes, a page per institution, program, curriculum (builder and template gallery), degree, term and subject, a page per assessment type, and a week view, a cross-subject assessments view and a grade report.

Every program parents to an institution or a self-taught path, two separate tables, and must resolve on create; below the program, formal and self-taught study are structurally identical, and Vida records study without ever credentialing it.
The Subjects-or-Courses display name (visual only), Education's view defaults and the calendar feed sync interval are Preferences keys that Education reads.

Studying a subject or topic is a study session the user can name and type, targeting the subject or topic; Education derives pace against the syllabus from completed study and class sessions, read live through Sessions, and never stores a copy.

Education has no due lane of its own; assessments and homework are due as tasks on Tasks' lane, class meetings are sessions on Sessions' agenda, and their reminders follow the base entity's push toggle.
A subject's weekly class pattern is Sessions' planned blocks targeting the subject, and the scheduling engine turns them into class sessions; Education keeps no recurrence of its own.
Education reads the books linked to a subject through Books' partition and their pace against the next class or assessment; it never reads every plan as if it were the subject's.
Education reads a subject's mastery from Knowledge through the Knowledge Subject linked to it, and an unlinked subject reads the deny-safe all-null mastery, never a throw.
Education's journal contribution reports the day's class sessions and due assessments, live and read on demand, and the journal registers it once the root composes Education.

Education's own journal blocks (today's classes, the assessments due, recent grades) are inline blocks the journal page holds and switches on, read live; the editor's classesBlock placeholder becomes the classes block.

Education exposes its subjects, grades, assessments and their components, and their events (an assessment recorded, a grade below a mark, homework not done by its date), as measurement sources and rule subjects that Purposes and Gamification read live; nothing copies Education's data.
The data model's record shows the Education tables migration 024 built (fifteen tables, the class extension excluded from the entity types, no foreign keys, deleted_at on eleven).

A subject routes up its chain (curriculum, an optional term, a degree tier); a given curriculum or term must resolve to a live, consistent chain or the create is a typed UnroutedSubjectError, skipped levels collapse, and a subject with no routing yet is allowed and organized later.

Grading-scale presets, program and curriculum catalogs, an institution list and term and holiday calendars ship as opt-in default datasets the user accepts or declines, refreshed as a whole set and read from a local copy; the pattern is built even when declined.

Education builds on other modules' entities instead of copying them; a class and a study block are sessions, a term is a dated container, and an assessment and homework are tasks of an Education type extended with Education's fields, each anchored in the hierarchy the syllabus and the program's setup define (its subject and the module or topic it covers) and linked to the Knowledge entities the user studies for it; being tasks gives them a due date and completion, and Education adds what tasks lack, such as preparation (ED-37).

When the root composes Education, it passes its deps (sessions, the session registry, spaces, notes, tasks, books, knowledge, effects) and Education registers its class sub_type, its journal contribution, its measurement sources and its read provider; nothing is wired centrally.
Education registers a read provider on the shared view registry, so the Tasks aggregator and any view resolve a subject; Tasks' course parent and Education's subject meet in one key.

A subject's grade reads on its system's scale (letter, 0-10, pass or fail, or the user's own), and the term and curriculum averages weight each subject by its credits through the engine's weighted rollup.

The user sets a manually measured subject's or program's progress, and a subject measured by deliverables, a goal or a count derives through the engine by its kind, so a subject with no grading system still measures.

Document extraction (a syllabus to the schedule and assessments) is an opt-in scoped extract whose model call runs on the device or in the cloud as egress, bounds the untrusted document's provenance, marks its rows source ai, and is never an agent.

The user prepares inside Learning following the hierarchy; preparation (study sessions they schedule, reminders, and sessions scheduled automatically over a timeframe before a due or meeting date) is set on a program and passed down to its courses, classes, assessments, homework and the Knowledge structure tied to them, and any entity below can override it; each session targets the item and the subject, module, topic and Knowledge entities it covers.

A class is a session of a subject, the class sub_type with its one-to-one extension, the base session owning time and lifecycle; assessments, grades, documents, homework and notes attach to the subject, never to a meeting, and a retake is a new subject in a new term.

Each subject has one schedule, fed by exactly one of three sources (calendar feed sync, document extraction or manual shaping); the meetings and the weekly view derive from it and never read a feed directly.

A calendar feed fetches on the device every sync interval as a user-added source under its external grant; events dedup by feed and uid and are ignored rather than deleted, unmatched events wait for a manual match, a failed fetch is kept in last error and never leaves a silently stale schedule, revoking a feed stops future fetches and keeps synced events, and the server never sees feed plaintext.

A grading system (per institution, program or subject override) defines weighted components and a scale; a subject's grade and any term or curriculum average derive from assessments through the nearest system, components that don't sum to 100% are flagged and never normalized, and a partial result is flagged, never hand-set or fabricated.

An assessment (exam, quiz, test, presentation or work) sits in the Learning hierarchy where the syllabus and the program's setup place it, under its subject and the module or topic it covers, never free of its parent; it carries its date, weight or points, modality and score, recording a result writes the score only and the grade re-derives, and rows auto-recorded from extraction carry source ai.

Homework is a task owned by Tasks that sits in the Learning hierarchy where the syllabus and the program's setup place it, under its subject and the module or topic it covers, never free of its parent, and Education reads it through the Tasks-to-Education read; Education never keeps a homework table or reads the tasks table.
Every missing or negative input denies egress (no user initiation, an unresolved target, external_out off, a missing sensitive consent, no per-target consent); only an explicit match permits.
An egress target keys on the stable integration identity, not a raw address, so upgrading a user's connector to a native one keeps its grants and audit.
external_out_ok never permits alone; per-target consent, the union and never-auto-transmit still gate on top, and a blanket allow-external never satisfies egress.
A slice that reads a sensitive module egresses only when both its sensitive consent and the external_out grant pass.
A fetch goes through the same egress gate, its address and parameters becoming the audited slice; a fetch with no sensitive read is governed by the grant alone.
Every egress needs proof the user started it; one composed by an agent or by code denies, and each hop to a cloud model meets the gate again.
The audit record names the target, a summary of the slice, the sensitive tags and the time, never the payload, and is field-encrypted and append-only when stored.
Checking an egress is pure and records nothing, and asserting one records it exactly once when permitted.
A capability the enforcer can't resolve is a programming error that propagates, not a policy denial, and a denial names the capability.
The guard decides and builds the record but holds no token and makes no provider call, and until real reach its consent default denies and its audit sink does nothing.
Flashcards owns only the card content entity and its interaction; scheduling, curves, the review log, grouping and mastery belong to the generic engine.
Flashcards is the framework's reference implementation, not its seam; it implements the study-method service anatomy and adds no roles or integration points of its own.
A drill earns and signals like any review; every recorded review, whichever study method records it, takes one path and fans out the same events.
Each card type (basic, reversed, cloze, image occlusion) validates its own content at author time with a typed error, declares how it renders, and declares how a review is scored.
Flashcards' surfaces (the card view, the drill, browse and manage, stats) show empty, loading, error and populated states, and an empty queue says all caught up.

A card is a reviewable scheduled by Knowledge's engine; its due state and curve live in the binding and the review state, never on the card, and the user binds a curve with `SM-2` as the swappable default.

The old deck table, the scheduling columns on cards and the card-review table are retired; grouping is a Knowledge object, caps sit on the binding, the resource is a link, and reviews are generic review events.
A deck is whichever entity below a topic the user designates, never a fixed entity.
A drill runs as a review session, and its outcomes are recorded as generic review events, one per card reviewed.
On review Flashcards emits outcomes as review events and Knowledge derives mastery; Flashcards never computes mastery or writes a schedule, even to recover from an engine gap.
Gathering is first-class; cards can be generated from definition objects, Book quotes and notes, and the source is kept as a link, so a later source delete leaves the card and its link intact.
Every card is taggable through the shared tag primitive, links to notes and pages, and carries media attachments.
The due queue is read from Knowledge's provider; Flashcards exposes no queue of its own and owns no daily caps, which belong to the binding.
Fiscal-legal is a Finance sub-context that composes Finance, Projects, Purposes and Tasks, Notifications and Calendar, owning only its own situation.
A modeled fiscal outcome feeds Purposes long-run planning through the ADR-011 contributions rails.
The guarded capabilities are opt-in, revocable and fail-closed; SITUATE and TRACK work by hand without them.
Obligation derivation and what-if run on-device; a cloud advisement is the only sharing path, scope-minimized and egress-gated.
AI-authored output carries source = ai and the not-professional-advice label.
User fiscal-legal free text and amounts are [E]; rule-packs are public plaintext; codes, types, dates and FKs are structural.

External and model paths follow the ADR-014/015 grant and scope contract with no new grant table; Fiscal and Legal's advice is a scoped one-shot model call, never an agent, while Finance offers its tools to outside agents through the gateway like every module.
Fiscal-legal has a UI surface; none exists or was planned.
The OS situates, tracks and models but never files; filing hands off to a professional or a third-party engine.
Every advisement, what-if and obligation is labeled not professional advice, and nothing on legal or tax matters auto-acts.
SITUATE (residency and money-touch) is the user's own [E] data computed on-device with no external integration.
Rule-packs come from the ADR-014 public-reference layer, device-mediated, whole-set, signed and versioned, gated by external_in_ok.
Obligations are derived on-device and surfaced as Tasks, Notifications and Calendar entries.
Advise and what-if ride ADR-015 (on_device or a disclosed, scope-minimized cloud egress) and are informational only.
A legal entity is a Project or linked to one; personal and entity fiscal situations are tracked apart and viewable together.
Money-touch is a jurisdiction link on Finance entities, which stay unchanged in structure.
Monetary values and identifying text are encrypted [E] (ZK-1); enums, currency, dates and flags stay plaintext.
Categories resolve to a managed list plus free-text subcategory; tags use the shared entity_tags, not inline JSON.
Deleting an account cascades its transactions and unlinks transfer targets and investments; soft delete hides without destroying.
Every create, edit, import and transfer succeeds locally first; devices reconcile LWW on structured columns.
Budgeting and liability-payment tracking are in scope but have no data model yet; no rule assumes their internals.
Commitments is a management layer derived from existing entities (no table), with direction and progress to a total from the ledger.
Finance owns the store tree that organizes money-holders and lockable reward-target boxes, never copying a balance.
Finance executes the move_money effect as an idempotent ledger movement; a penalty locks a box and never destroys money.

Finance views are the switchable dashboard, account pages with nested views, all-transactions with a timeframe page, and the all-assets, all-investments and all-liabilities pages with the liability-payment view.
Finance has an import and reconcile wizard screen and a bank or broker connection screen.
Money is integer cents and rates are basis points; no floats for money.
An account balance is derived as opening_balance plus the signed ledger, never hand-edited.
A transfer is one row with a distinct destination and is excluded from every income and expense aggregate.
Recurring transactions forecast by default; materializing real rows on the due date is opt-in and editable before confirm.
Net worth, investment value and monthly totals are computed client-side; storing them is an opt-in the user owns.
Net worth is the account balances plus asset values minus liability balances, in the base currency.
Holdings keep their own currency; totals convert with device-side or manual FX rates, never fetched by the server.
External ingestion is device-only under ADR-014 (X1/X5/X8); imports reconcile through import_staging and commit only on user confirm.

Nothing in Vida requires the System; it runs only when the user turns feature_gamification on, and then any action can earn or lose a consequence that the System surfaces; it is the motivation partner to Purposes, never a gate on core function.

The System reads behavioral signals only through the measurement sources the owning modules advertise and stores none of them; a missing or stale source suppresses the rule with a typed flag and never fires on made-up data.

Streaks are module-owned (Habits, Routines, Check-ins, Relationships' interactions); the System reads each one through its measurement source and awards milestone consequences, and never computes or stores a streak.

The overloaded profile splits by single writer; the System keeps only each currency's total and level, the check-in streak goes to Check-ins, persona, motivation, modules and onboarding go to Preferences, and personal details stay in the profile until an account model exists, so no field ends with two writers.

An achievement is a measurable predicate (a streak or count of at least N, a level reached, net worth of at least a sum) evaluated on the measurement sources, the consequence events and a reconcile pass, never a bespoke checker; the app curates the catalogue.
A level is a pure function of a currency's lifetime total over a fixed non-linear curve with titles; it never de-levels on a spend.

The System gives the journal a contribution for the day (currency earned and locked, achievements unlocked, level-ups) and raises a notification on an unlock, a level-up or a consequence through surface_notification; Notifications reading it is its only in-edge.
Persona weighting, module guidance and template suggestions belong to Preferences, Onboarding and Spaces templates; the System at most reads persona to frame its rewards.
A quest or challenge is a time-boxed saved view over rules and goals in Spaces, never a bespoke quest table.

Currency names, box and store names, rule and user-authored achievement titles and descriptions, and ledger notes are encrypted client-side [E]; enums, amounts, levels, timestamps and references stay plaintext. M1 is a pass-through.

Every earn, lock, spend and consequence succeeds locally first; structured columns merge last-writer-wins, and the ledger converges on the deterministic effect event key, so a consequence never applies twice across devices.

A rule is a measured condition and a consequence; the condition is an acyclic event-trigger or derived-pull binding, and the consequence dispatches separate typed effects (grant_currency with award_xp as its experience case, lock_currency, move_money, surface_notification), each in its own Additive write class, never one umbrella effect or a new engine.
A failed money move or consequence leaves state unchanged and flags it; a retry never double-applies, and a penalty never silently over-applies.

Gamification registers the award_xp handler with the grant and lock handlers when it is composed; a feeder's award_xp carries no amount, and the handler grants experience points from the shipped-default reward rule for that feeder's event (static seed, not synced, deterministic, weighted by difficulty or priority under the Preferences default), so a feeder never decides its own reward; the user can retune or replace those defaults with rules of their own (GM-36).

Gamification's rules hear the signals other modules emit (a project, milestone, purpose, target or task completed, a reading session ended, a review or assessment recorded) as events keyed by source and transition, derive the entity from the target reference, and reward or penalize it through shipped or user rules; the emitter grants nothing itself.

Derived-pull rules and achievements are evaluated on each consequence event and by a reconcile pass on a recurring occasion, each fire keyed by its occasion so a recurring rule fires once per occasion and a missed event is caught up; a rule over something that didn't happen is checked when its window closes (a homework not done by its due date, fewer pages read than set by the end of the week).
The user edits and archives a currency they defined; an archived currency keeps its ledger and stops taking new consequences, and a shipped currency can't be archived.
A currency's level reports its title and the progress to the next level, over a curve and title bands kept as config rather than code.
Reaching a level can unlock a reward that does something, granted once per level and kept when the balance is later spent.
The user authors their own achievements and challenges over any entity in Vida under the capability sandbox, on the same predicates as the curated catalogue.
A rule's condition can combine several bindings, all or any, on the economy's rules and the capability-authoring rail, never a second automation engine.

Gamification advertises each currency's derived quantities and level as measurement sources, so a derived-pull rule, an achievement or a user's measurement override can read them, and the acyclic guard covers those edges.

The economy runs many user-definable currencies at once, each backed by real money (through Finance), a self-granted allowance (a vacation day, a cheat meal, hours of play, no wealth needed) or measured time, and a reward or penalty can be denominated in any of them.
The journal contribution reads the day itself, the currency earned and locked, the achievements unlocked and the level-ups on that local day, not a snapshot of totals.
The journal of the day shows Gamification through its own inline blocks, live and worked from, never one summary block.
Gamification serves its rules, achievements and currencies as a read provider in the shared view registry, so a challenge view (GM-17) and other saved views resolve them.

In the app the composition root composes Gamification behind feature_gamification with the rail, the effect registry, the shared measurement sources and the capability enforcer, and Gamification registers its effect handlers, its journal contribution and its read provider.
The consequence ledger is readable as an activity history per currency, newest first, so the user sees what earned, locked or spent each amount.
The curated achievement and challenge library ships as an opt-in default dataset the user accepts or declines; it refreshes as a whole set and is read from a local copy.

Any entity in Vida can be a rule's subject; the user picks an entity type or one entity from any module (a task, a homework, a grade, a book's pages, a study session, a habit) and rewards or penalizes what they choose, an event that happened, a measure crossing a threshold, or something that didn't happen by a deadline or within a period; the shipped feeders and rules are defaults and examples, never the limit.
Each currency's to-distribute, earned, locked and current quantities derive from the consequence ledger on read; stored totals and levels are caches, never the source of truth.

A penalty locks currency or money into a held, recoverable pool through a lock_currency or move_money effect and never destroys it; a penalty that would drive a balance below its floor clamps and flags.

A real-money reward is a transfer into a storage box through Finance's guarded handler, a real entry in the user's own ledger and never a bank call; a self-granted allowance needs no Finance, and a Finance or Health write needs the user's explicit capability consent.
A reward routed into a storage box can earmark a Dream or a Purpose, so the consequence ladders into that goal's progress, which Purposes reads from the box through Finance.

Rules can be user-authored; shipped rules are trusted, and a user-authored rule runs headless under the capability sandbox (declare, grant, enforce, revocable, failing closed), reusing that machinery without being a render block.

Storage is a Finance-owned single-parent tree of group and wrapper nodes over existing accounts, investments and assets, with a lock flag, a dream or purpose earmark and a currency overlay; each money-holder is wrapped once, any other grouping is a Spaces tag, and net worth is the tree minus liabilities.

A habit's name, description, unit, cue, reward and success_criteria and a completion's location are encrypted client-side [E]; habit_type, frequency, days_of_week, domain, time_of_day and the counters are plaintext config, and tags are entity_tags rows, not an inline column. M1 is a pass-through.

The user may log or edit a completion for a past date, which recomputes the streak; a future date, or a date beyond the backfill window, is rejected with a typed BackfillWindowError and writes nothing.
Deleting a habit deletes its habit_completions; a soft delete hides the habit and keeps its ledger until the hard delete.

Every create, edit, complete and backfill succeeds locally first with a co-transactional sync_queue row; structured columns reconcile Last-Writer-Wins across devices, and the completion ledger merges by habit and date.

A habit is a pursuable with measurement_kind (natural rate, how often it happens) and binding_mode (a completion is the event trigger); it has no bespoke goal-type column, and its rate and progress derive on read.
Each time in a due habit's times_of_day becomes a reminder, gated by the Preferences push_habits toggle; Habits feeds the Sessions due agenda that Notifications reads (HB-6's reminder half).

The backfill window is a user setting that Preferences owns (habit_backfill_window_days), set in Settings and read by Habits through its Preferences port; unset means no limit, never a hidden default (HB-10's window half).

A done completion fires `award_xp` after the commit, once per habit and date, from every log, detailed log, backfill or edit that leaves it done; in the app the habits service is composed with the effect rail and the tag resolver.
A failed completion effect never fails the completion, and it is flagged for retry, never dropped silently.
A custom frequency needs days_of_week; a create or a patch without it is refused with HabitScheduleError, since the habit could never be due.
The v1 fields are restored, success_criteria and difficulty (very_easy to very_hard) on a habit and location and completion_time on a completion.

A streak is the run of consecutive scheduled occurrences that are done, and an elapsed scheduled miss resets it to 0 with no grace; current_streak, longest_streak and total_completions are a cache recomputed from the habit_completions ledger on every log, edit, delete and backfill, never adjusted by hand.
Habits tags through the shared entity_tags primitive with entity_type habit, never an inline tag list, and reads a habit's tags through the association resolver, which returns none when absent.
project_habits stays a live junction that links a habit to projects; linking again restores a removed link, and only the purpose junctions retire into contributions.
The journal's daily summary pulls the habits due and done on the day through the Habits journal contribution; Habits never pushes to the journal.
Habits serves a habit's streak and completion rate as measures that Journal and Purposes read through the measurement seam, never a table read.

Habits has four surfaces, the Dashboard (check off any habit), today's list in Calendar, List and Checkbox modes, the per-habit page (streak, completion rate and mood charts, a calendar of completions and the linked note page) and the All-Habits Overview.

Every Habits surface renders its terminal states (today's list, Dashboard and Overview, quick and detailed log, analytics, backfill, the per-habit page); a failed log or backfill reverts and shows a typed error.
React Query owns habit reads and writes, with optimistic completion logging, and Zustand owns the ephemeral screen state (active view and today mode, per-habit tab, detailed-log draft, selection).

A Routines habit step completes its habit through the Habits contract, one native tick per occurrence on the habit's own ledger; the habit stays the single source of truth and fires its own completion effects, and a missing habit or a date beyond the backfill window fails the step loudly.

Habits serves a completion grid of every active habit across a date range, each day carrying whether it is scheduled, its count and whether it is done, in one ledger read; the Global Calendar draws its habits from it.

Habits handles complete_habit_occurrence, the effect a session or a consequence fires to complete a habit occurrence; the handler logs it through the Habits completion path as one keyed write per habit and date, so the streak and the habit's own effects move once, and a missing habit or a date beyond the backfill window fails loudly; a habit's own completion never fires it.
A habit has at most one completion per date; logging a date already logged updates that row, never adds a second.
For a build habit a completion means it was done; for a break habit it means the user abstained that day, so a break streak counts clean scheduled days and a day with no completion is the relapse.

A habit is done for the day when count reaches target_count, and over-achieving still counts as done; a partial is logged for analytics but never advances the streak, and value is a measured quantity for analytics only.
Today's list holds the active habits whose frequency and days_of_week match today, computed on read, never stored, and shown grouped by time_of_day.
Mood before and after, ease and satisfaction (each 1 to 5) are optional and captured only by an explicit detailed log; the default completion is a single tap.

Habits pushes nothing to Purposes; a purpose, goal or dream a habit relates to reads the habit's completions through the Habits service and computes them into that day's progress, and Habits never writes purpose data.
A done completion grants experience points through `award_xp`, applied by Gamification as `grant_currency(XP)` into the consequence_ledger, once per habit and date; Habits never writes points itself.

Every tracked attribute is one metric of kind body-measure, performance-capacity, test-result or biomarker, with a unit, a direction (higher or lower is better), a category and an optional side (left, right or bilateral); the biomarker kind ships an editable starter clinical panel, and there are no separate body, performance or test systems.

All Health data is encrypted (most fields), and every external or model path (wearable sync, food database, barcode, photo analysis, plan or meal generation, prescription import) is opt-in, on-device-preferred and at the user's own risk, never a precondition of the manual Core.
Weights, lengths and energy are stored canonical (kg, cm, kcal) and shown in the units the user picks in Preferences.
Testing and recovery protocols are Knowledge objects of a protocol kind, referenced by id, never Health tables.
Health composes Sessions, Knowledge, Notes and Pages, Spaces and Preferences and never rebuilds sessions, scheduling, tags, views or notes.

The user has full sovereignty over their own body; Health records, advises and safety-nets, but never gatekeeps, prescribes, credentials or blocks, with a one-time explicit acknowledgment and the user always free to proceed.

Danger signals (overtraining, extreme or rapid weight change, an extreme caloric deficit, a concerning biomarker, an injury or pain pattern, a warning response) raise an advisory safety flag, surfaced in Health and as a notification, that says when medical attention is warranted; a flag is dismissible, logged and never blocking.

Health owns the medical profile (conditions, allergies, injuries, medications, supplements, prescriptions, clearances, contraindications) and exposes it to both pillars; injuries filter exercises, allergies filter foods, prescriptions inform targets, and every filter advises, so an excluded item is flagged with a reason, never removed.
Medical data is the most sensitive class; every medical field is encrypted, imported doctor input is opt-in and on-device-preferred, and Vida never sends medical data in plaintext.

A prescription from a doctor, the community or the user may spawn an experiment to validate it on the user's own body; imported prescription content is untrusted input whose provenance travels into any model prompt, the outgoing slice is user-reviewed, and injected tool calls can't widen the scope.
Health Domains contain Health Factors, a user-extensible monitoring hierarchy with a shipped starter set that groups metrics; a factor result is a metric value, never a separate store.

A metric value enters by direct measure, derived computation, a test protocol or an exam result, and carries its provenance source (manual, photo, wearable, derived, exam, import or a model) with an optional photo and life-context; the source is the value's provenance, distinct from a goal's binding mode, and wearable or import values arrive only through device-mediated ingestion under the user's grant.

An exam (a blood panel, a checkup, imaging) is set up by the user with a schedule and reminders; each occurrence is a task of a Health exam type (an obligation when the schedule recurs) that reaches Today, the Calendar and reminders through Tasks, never a session, and Health extends it with the metrics it produces, so its results come back as metric values with the exam as their source.

Derived metrics (basal metabolic rate, energy expenditure, lean mass, fat mass, one-rep max) are computed on the device from other metric values by a formula declared on the metric, never by a model or a server; a stored value is a cache and the source rows are the truth.

External integrations are opt-in, bidirectional and intent-only for now; input from health platforms, wearables and open sources becomes metric values through device-mediated ingestion under the user's input grant, reconciled add-only, and output to medical systems is egress under the stricter guard (per-target consent, the union of consents, an audit, never sent automatically); neither is a precondition of the manual Core.
Biomarker ranges inform and flag, never diagnose, prescribe or block; they are soft context under autonomy with clarity, and biomarker data is the most sensitive class.

Health's surfaces show every capability's terminal states (metric series, monitoring, exams, goals, roles, experiments, the profile, the medical profile, safety flags), and the Training, Nutrition and role surfaces are Spaces (tags and saved views), never a hand-built page per pillar.
Health contributes its day to the journal (workouts done, meals and macros, calories burned and consumed, metrics logged), read live through its contribution.

Health has its own journal blocks and capability blocks, a workout logger and a photo food logger among them; each reads Health live and writes only through Health's service, separate from its journal contribution.

Health runs no due lane of its own; its due items ride their base entities, so an exam occurrence or a planned meal is due as a task and an assigned workout as a planned session, and they reach Today, the Calendar and reminders like any task or session, where the user's push toggles can gate a Health type.

Every Health entity is a potential Gamification rule subject; Health exposes its events (a workout done, a record set, an exam logged, a flag raised) and its measures (streaks, adherence, goal progress) so a user's rule can reward or penalize them, including something that didn't happen.
Health reads the user's subjective energy, mood and sleep from Check-ins live (Health owns the objective measures) and keeps no copy.

Health has one goal system, and the goal is the pursuable; it carries a measurement kind and a binding mode in place of a goal type, and its progress is a nullable override that derives on read from its target metrics or role mastery over a short, medium or long horizon, never hand-typed for a measurable goal.

Health's entity types register in the open taggable-type registry, so tags, links and pages reach every metric, goal, role, experiment, exam, medical entry, flag, food, meal, plan, exercise and workout; Health owns no tag table.
Health serves a read provider, so its entities show in views, search and links like any other module's.

When the root composes Health, Health registers its own session sub_types and task types, its effect handlers, its measurement sources, its journal contribution and its read provider; nothing is wired centrally.

The starter biomarker panel, the starter domains and factors, and the curated physical-role library ship as opt-in default datasets the user accepts or declines, refreshed as a whole set and read from a local copy; the pattern is built even when declined.
The data model's record shows the Health tables migrations 027-029 built (twelve Core, six Nutrition, five Training, no foreign keys, deleted_at only where the floor marks it).
The Health module toggle and the dietary defaults are Preferences keys that Health reads.

Health builds on other modules' entities instead of copying them; a workout is a session of a Health type, an exam occurrence and a planned meal are tasks of a Health type, each tracked Health's way with the fields and features the base entity lacks, and habits, routines and the other modules attach and link to Health entities (a supplement or medication habit, a routine's exercise step) as they do to any entity.

A goal drives programming; in the Core the user builds the training and nutrition plans by hand toward the goal, and model generation or library and prescription import are opt-in layers whose rows carry their source.

Body-metric series and goal progress are measurement sources (body weight, body fat, one-rep max per lift); Purposes and derived-pull goals read them through the measurement read seam, never a table read, and an outage keeps the last-known value with a flag.

The energy loop is closed and dynamic; calories burned come from the user's chosen method (a formula from duration, intensity and body weight by default, a wearable, or manual entry), the nutrition intake target recomputes against each day's burn, volume is sets times reps times weight, cardio is duration times intensity, and calories are protein and carbs at 4 and fat at 9 per gram.

An experiment states a hypothesis, defines a control arm and a test arm, runs for a duration, is measured through Health metrics and subjective responses, and resolves to a winner and a key learning; hypotheses come from the user, community claims or a doctor's prescription.

Responses and resolved experiments accumulate into a derived response profile (how this body responds to a training type, a food or a timing), computed on read and never a base table, which a planning model may take as context.

A physical role is the trainable-capability unit (calisthenics, swimming, a martial art, triathlon); it owns objectives, a can-do definition and a mastery that derives as a weighted rollup over its linked exercises and goals, generates or links the exercises that build it, binds a Knowledge subject and a Skill, reads the medical profile to exclude or adjust exercises, and is authored by hand or by opt-in model or curated import.

Ingredients hold atomic macros, a dish's macros are the sum of its ingredients, a meal's are the sum of its dishes, a day's total is the sum of its meals, and calories are protein and carbs at 4 and fat at 9 per gram; a dish never stores its macros as the truth.
Logged meals, macros and calories consumed reach the journal and the Core energy loop, adherence and goal progress reach Gamification, and meal reminders reach Notifications.

Allergies and intolerances from the medical profile filter foods and plans by their allergens, and conditions and prescriptions inform intake targets and the supplement protocol; filtering advises with a reason, never removes, and an imported prescription is a device-mediated ingest whose untrusted text carries provenance into any model prompt.

Ingredients and dishes carry a functional area (the eight body systems they serve, from digestive and gut to systemic resilience), so meals and plans can target a system; it is taggable, ships as an editable starter and is never hard-coded as truth.

Ingredients carry a whole-food type (leafy greens, cruciferous, roots, bioactive fruits, nuts and seeds, legumes, whole grains, animal proteins, spices, functional beverages) for grouping and filtering, as an editable starter.
A dish is documented data with an optional recipe page by default; only when the user turns on cooking tracking does a dish gain a learn-to-cook status as a Skill or Knowledge object.

Every external, model and tag path is layered; the food database and barcode are a device-mediated public-reference whole-set import under the input grant, a fetch without the grant fails closed with a typed error, meal generation and photo analysis are scoped model calls that fall back to manual and never act as an agent, every model row is tagged as model-sourced, and every Nutrition entity tags through the universal tags, never an inline column.

Nutrition's surfaces show their terminal states (empty libraries, a plan planning, active, on hold or completed, a day planned through modified, a meal planned through skipped or substituted, shopping needed through cancelled, a failed generation or photo falling back to manual).

The food-composition database and the functional-area and whole-food-type starters ship as opt-in default datasets the user accepts or declines, refreshed as a whole set and read from a local copy, and a barcode looks up that copy.

A planned meal is a task of a Health meal type, never a session; it reaches Today, the Calendar and reminders through Tasks, and Nutrition extends it with its dishes, macros, cost, satisfaction, photo and provenance.
The nutritional plan derives a calorie and macro target from the user's Health goals and recomputes it against each day's burn (a training day means eating more); a stored target is a cache.
A nutrition goal phase (fat loss, muscle gain, recomposition, event prep) is a Core Health goal; Nutrition references it and owns no parallel goal system.
Meal-timing, portion and food-choice tests and food responses are the Core adaptation engine's experiments and responses for the nutrition pillar.

A plan or a day's meal plan is built by hand, by an opt-in model call, or by import (a doctor's prescription included, then validated by an experiment), and the row carries its manual, model or import source; the manual path is always enough.
Shopping items and meal costs, in integer cents, bridge to Finance's budget, and the shopping list derives from the day's or period's meal plan.
Meals and responses carry a life-context (normal, training, rest, travel, social, sick), so intake and analysis are schedule- and travel-aware.
